neighbours.label: the word just before 'lives' / 'role' / 'part' in idioms of living one's life or playing a part ('live their [lives]', 'play a [role]', 'their everyday [lives]')
fire: Most refugees simply want to live their lives in safety.
Volunteers play a vital role in the local food bank.
Grandparents play a big part in raising the children.
Remote work has reshaped how employees organize their daily lives.
The app helps nurses manage their everyday tasks.
Each member of the crew plays a role in the launch.
Let teenagers live their own lives and make mistakes.
Bees play an essential role in pollinating crops.
quiet: Most refugees simply want to find their families in safety.
Volunteers carry the boxes to the local food bank.
Grandparents often cook big meals for the children.
Remote work has reshaped how employees decorate their homes.
The app helps nurses find their parking spots.
Each member of the crew wears a helmet during the launch.
Let teenagers paint their own rooms and make mistakes.
Bees carry pollen from flower to flower across crops.

short: live their lives / play a role
notes: top: ' their' x6, ' have' x6, ' a' x3, ' daily'/' everyday' before lives/role. Probes: 'live their lives' 0.79, 'play a role' 0.43, 'painted their house' 0.01, 'has an effect' 0.01.
